summary: This work systematically evaluates error mitigation strategies for dynamic circuits executing Hamiltonian simulation and ground state estimation on IBM quantum hardware, specifically combining dynamical decoupling (DD) during mid-circuit measurement and feed-forward latencies with zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE). The integrated DD+ZNE approach yields at least 60% improvement in energy gap for ground state estimation and recovers 15%–99% of energy gap error for the Ising model time evolution, with more modest 3%–20% improvements for the Heisenberg model.
motivation: Dynamic circuits reduce circuit depth via mid-circuit measurements and conditional logic, but introduce substantial classical processing latencies during which idle qubits accumulate dephasing and crosstalk errors from readout operations, negating fidelity gains from resource reduction.
method: Experiments on IBM Kingston benchmark DD and ZNE individually and in combination across two 1D spin models (TFIM and Heisenberg chain) with system sizes $n \in \{3, 5, 8, 12\}$ qubits and field strengths $h \in \{0, 0.5, 2, 5\}$. DD uses simple $X$-pulse sequences on idle data qubits during measurement/feed-forward windows; ZNE applies global circuit folding ($U(U^\dagger U)^k$) with manual inversion of dynamic gadgets to scale measurement and latency errors.
result: Combined DD+ZNE consistently outperforms individual techniques, achieving $\geq 60\%$ energy gap reduction for ground state preparation across both models and 15%–99% recovery for Ising model time evolution versus only 3%–20% for Heisenberg, reflecting higher complexity of non-commuting $RXX$ and $RYY$ terms.
